defects_are_synthetic: An E0 defect is a perturbation THIS STUDY injected into a sound published manuscript. No number in this file asserts that any real paper contains an error. Manuscripts appear only as opaque labels.
what_this_is: Audited aggregate results that support the fair-scoring analysis but are not per-cell quantities. Unlike fair_scoring_cells.json, the intervals here were computed by the frozen analysis and are reproduced verbatim; a visitor cannot regenerate them from the counts on this page.

scorer_audit.design: 30 relation-targeted E0 cells the frozen scorer marked as misses were sampled under a stratified, non-proportional design across three strata and rated independently by six colleagues. A stratum's measured rate is reweighted back to the stratum's share of the corpus before it is reported.

strata.A_NO_FINDINGS: the system returned no finding at all
strata.B_OFF_TARGET: the system returned findings, none about the tested relation
strata.C_NEAR_MISS: the system returned a finding arguably about the tested relation

headline_false_negative_rate.interval_is: static audited aggregate, not recomputed in your browser

counts.note: Two units, both correct and not interchangeable: an ITEM is one sampled miss resolved by majority across six reviewers; a JUDGMENT is one reviewer's answer on one item. Rates quoted per item and per judgment differ for that reason, not because they disagree.

agreement.prevalence_caveat: Most items are true scorer misses, so agreement is measured against a skewed base rate; kappa is reported with raw agreement rather than instead of it. Per-reviewer and per-pair figures are NOT published: six identifiable colleagues produced them.

scorer_audit.e1_near_misses_were_not_audited: The audit sampled E0 misses only. The 61 E1 near misses received NO human rating. Any scenario that corrects the E1 side applies the E0-measured rate to unaudited cells, which is a modelling assumption and is labelled as one.

scenarios.basis: Every majority-Yes human judgment is credited as a scorer false negative on E0, with NO offsetting correction on E1. This is the reading most generous to the criticism of the scorer.
scenarios.description: measured majority-Yes rate credited on E0 only; most generous to the criticism

scenarios.basis: Majority-Yes AND majority-Partially credited on E0 only. The outer bound of the criticism.
scenarios.description: Yes plus Partially credited on E0 only; the outer bound of the criticism

scenarios.basis: The measured rate is APPLIED to E1 near misses as well as E0 detections. The E1 side was never audited by a human, so this side of the correction is modelled, not measured.
scenarios.description: measured rate applied to E0 detections AND E1 near misses

scenarios.basis: Yes plus Partially applied to both states. The E1 side is modelled, not measured.
scenarios.description: Yes plus Partially applied to both states

verdict.dprime_caveat: Under the ONE-SIDED outer bound the d' difference falls to +0.054 with a 95% CI of [-0.347, 0.438], which INCLUDES ZERO. The d' difference therefore does not survive the most generous possible reading of the criticism, although the balanced-accuracy difference does. Under the symmetric correction, which is the more defensible of the two because it applies the same leniency to both states, d' is +0.714 (95% CI [0.388, 1.041]) and excludes zero. This split must be reported, not resolved by choosing the convenient scenario.
verdict.reasoning: The measured scorer false-negative rate is 13.14% of relation-targeted misses (95% CI 4.38-21.9%), stratum-reweighted. That is material rather than negligible, which is why the status is not a clean SCORER_VALIDATED. But even under the outer bound of the criticism (crediting every majority-Yes AND majority-Partially on E0, with no offsetting correction on E1), the balanced-accuracy difference remains +6.16 pp (95% CI [1.46, 10.59]) and d' remains +0.054 (95% CI [-0.347, 0.438]). Plausible strict-scorer false negatives therefore do NOT explain the fair-scoring interface difference in balanced accuracy. The d' difference is the more fragile of the two: see dprime_caveat.
verdict.why_not_fully_validated: a 13.14% false-negative rate on misses is real and must be disclosed; the strict matcher understates relation-targeted discovery
verdict.one_sided_is_conservative_because: the pooled open-weight data contain 61 E1 near misses against 12 scored false alarms, so applying leniency to E0 alone flatters the relation-targeted rung; the symmetric scenarios show the difference is larger when both states are corrected

anthropic.scope: existing records only; no new Anthropic request was issued in this phase

accuracy.note: The three readings differ in how many of the 60 are scoreable, not in the scoring rule. No reading changes a verdict that the strict parser already read.

anthropic.finding_list_rungs_conclusion: Every finding-list request that reached the provider was refused. The interface is not measurable under the frozen prompt, which is why this phase issues no further Anthropic requests.
anthropic.refusals_are_not_failures: A policy refusal is the provider declining to produce a response. It is an interface and availability fact, not evidence about verification ability, and it is reported separately rather than scored as an error.
anthropic.parser_note: The strict frozen parser accepts only a correctly fenced JSON object. A looser parser that scans for the outermost braces recovers 6 further records; both readings are reported, and the scoring rule is identical in each. The parser is not tuned after seeing the results.
